title: api-config-deployment-routing-sketch
content:
Purpose:
Sketching routing and deployment config ideas for model variant fallbacks, cost-aware routing, and cache-aware batching. Mostly notes to self and questions for Samir/Casey before turning into a readable PRD.

Scope:
- Hosted API + Dedicated + Private (same surface)
- Route by: latency SLO, cost tier, region, model capability (exact vs approx), and fallback policies
- Integrate with KV/prefix cache so that hot prefixes bias towards faster (higher-cost) endpoints

High-level goals:
1) Allow fine-grained per-route policy that composes: primary model, fallback chain, cost thresholds, and cache affinity.
2) Make fallback safe: degrade deterministically (model size, quant, or capability) and provide observability & synthetic checks.
3) Support multi-tenant Dedicated with reserved capacity while enabling overflow to hosted with cost control.

Rough config sketch (yaml-ish):

route: text-generation/reply
primary:
  model: redwood/rlhf-13b
  deployment: dedicated-us-west-1
  latency_slo_ms: 120
  cost_limit_per_1000_tokens_usd: 0.80
fallback_chain:
  - model: redwood/rlhf-7b-quant
    deployment: hosted
    reason: "cost_or_capacity"
    max_latency_ms: 300
  - model: redwood/llama-3-6b
    deployment: hosted
    reason: "capacity"
    max_latency_ms: 500
cache_affinity:
  kv_prefix_keys: [user_prompt_hash, convo_topic]
  prefer_cached_on: dedicated-us-west-1  # prefer routing to deployment that holds warm KV cache
  cache_warm_threshold_ms: 50
burst_policy:
  allow_overflow_to_hosted: true
  overflow_budget_tokens: 1e6
  throttle_if_cost_exceeded: true

Questions / open decisions:
- How do we reliably express "capability" differences? (e.g., hallucination risk threshold)
  - Option: attach eval vectors / capability tags to model metadata and require policy match.
  - TODO: convo with Research to design small capability taxonomy.

- Prefetch / cache warming: who owns the warm-up? Route-level controller or Dedicated infra?
  - Idea: on canary/fallover events, trigger async warm-up jobs to fill KV caches on target deployment.

- Metrics & SLOs to expose:
  - per-route: p50/p95 latency, fallback_rate, cost_per_1k_tokens, cache_hit_rate, quality_regressions
  - per-deployment: capacity_utilization, average_queue_time, active_models

- Safety: telemetry should flag when fallback occurs > X% and correlate with quality evals.

Operational flow (sketch):
1) Request arrives -> route lookup by API path + tenant policies
2) Evaluate candidate deployments (affinity by region, cache presence, reserved capacity)
3) Score candidates by: meets_latency_slo ? 0 : penalty; cost_estimate; cache_bonus; capacity_headroom
4) If top candidate is overloaded or cost limit exceeded, iterate down fallback_chain
5) If routed to non-primary, emit fallback event, and optionally trigger cache/warm-up for primary

Scoring pseudocode:
score = 1000
if est_latency > latency_slo_ms: score -= (est_latency - latency_slo_ms) * 2
score -= (cost_est_usd_per_1k_tokens - cost_limit) * 1000  # big penalty if exceeding cost budget
score += cache_hit_bonus  # prefer cached endpoints
score += (reserved_capacity ? 50 : 0)

Notes about cache_affinity: if we bias strongly to endpoints that have warm KV prefix caches, latency drops dramatically for common prefixes. But cache residency is dynamic -> need fast signals. Idea: maintain a lightweight cache-heatstore: map[prefix_hash] -> {deployment_ids, last_seen_ts, hit_rate} (TTL 24h).

Privacy/Private-deployments note:
- For Private/VPC deployments, routing must not leak model metadata or routing decision payloads to hosted telemetry. We should support a lightweight routing token that contains policy decisions but redacts prompt content.

Testing plan for rollout:
- Unit tests for policy evaluation engine (score calc)
- Sinlge-route canary: route 1% to new policy + synthetic traffic that asserts latency and fallback_rate < 2%
- Regression: prompt-set evals comparing primary vs fallback for quality delta; auto-block if quality drop > threshold (x BLEURT/ROUGE proxy)

Immediate action items (me):
- [ ] Validate config shape with API/Console team (Samir)
- [ ] Add capability-tag proposal doc and ping Research (Olivia)
- [ ] Prototype lightweight cache-heatstore (Casey)
- [ ] Wire up fallback telemetry event (minimal fields: route, tenant, primary_model, fallback_model, reason, latency_ms, cost_est_usd)

Links / refs:
- RED-2147: dedicated overflow behaviour
- GH PR #482: initial route-config proto + schema

Notes to self (casual):
- Keep the config small and composable. People will hate YAML that repeats. Introduce templates (route recipes) for common patterns: low-cost, low-latency, high-quality.
- Think about UI: route editor should surface fallback chain and a simple simulation panel (simulate 3 sample prompts -> show decisions).

End of sketch.

(Will tidy up and move to product PRD after aligning with Samir + Casey.)
